messages.text:
Estimado Luis:

La maestra que nos mandó las fotos de su huerto hizo también una versión del cartel para las familias. Se la adjunto porque a dos personas del consejo les gustó cómo se ve el título y me preguntaron si podríamos usar esa misma letra en los encabezados de la página de donativos.

En el cartel dice Sauce Display. No sé si viene con el programa en el que lo hizo la maestra o si ella la compró por su cuenta. ¿La podríamos usar sin que se vuelva otro gasto para la Fundación? Si complica la salida de la página, con que me diga eso tengo para contestarles.

Con aprecio,
Lucía Herrera

Mtra. Lucía Herrera Domínguez
Directora General | Fundación Semilla Viva A.C.
Huertos escolares en la Ciudad de México

Estimada Lucía:

Qué bonito quedó el cartel, la maestra tiene buen ojo. Para la página, sin embargo, le recomiendo quedarnos con la tipografía que ya aprobamos.

En el PDF el título viene convertido en imagen, así que no sé de dónde sacó la maestra Sauce Display ni con qué permiso. Para usarla en la página habría que comprar una licencia para web a nombre de la Fundación, y eso sí sería un gasto más.

El cartel puede quedarse como está para las familias. Que convivan las dos letras no es problema.

Saludos,
Luis

Luis Cordero
Diseño de marca y producto
hola@luiscordero.example · +44 7700 900 418

truth.summary: Luis mantiene la tipografía aprobada para la página de donativos porque no se sabe si la letra del cartel tiene licencia para web.
facts: La tipografía del cartel se llama Sauce Display.
El título del PDF está guardado como imagen.
El cartel adjunto corresponde al huerto de la Primaria Leona Vicario.

subject: Cupboard by the Albion Court side door

messages.text:
Dear all,

When we last took the book club chairs back to Albion Court, two of us waited by the side door while the third went round to find the key.  We are keen to avoid repeating that performance, which took most of the interval between the rain beginning and the rain becoming serious.

The managing agent now says the low cupboard beside that door is for the meter readers only.  I am certain we were told we could leave the six folding chairs there, and I seem to remember it was Luis who sorted it out for us.  Does anyone still have the agent’s letter?  It was about the cupboard, rather than general permission to use the hall, and the last thing I want is for somebody to spend an evening looking for the wrong document.

The chairs can stay where they are until we hear.  If they do need to go, I can fit them in my hall for a week; they are the wooden ones with the little brass handle near the hinge.

Yours,
Hamish Fairweather

Evening all,

If they do have to go I can carry all six round to Hamish’s on Sunday. Someone will have to let me in though, I’ve no key for any of it.

K

Hello all,

I was with Joan this morning and we went down to look. The chairs are still in the low cupboard, right against the far wall. There was enough room to get to the meter, but you have to pull the door all the way open to do it. The note stuck to the inside of the door says the floor in front of the meter has to stay clear. I didn’t see anything about the rest of the cupboard.

Joan still has the square key in the dish with the bus passes. If you need it on Sunday could you ring before you go round? She can manage the latch but the buzzer sends her all the way to the far end of the flat, which she is doing quite slowly at the moment.

Harriet

Harriet Lowe MCSP
Dalston Step Clinic, Dalston

I think the agent’s letter is in the Albion folder somewhere, still in a box here. They called it the low store, which might be why nothing comes up when you search for chairs. I’ll look for the paper copy over the weekend.

Dear all,

That is exactly the phrase I couldn’t think of.  Luis, would you scan the page with the actual permission if you find it?  The agent’s woman on the phone said an old letter would do so long as it names the cupboard.  A photograph is fine if the printer is still in a box.  I’ll leave Sunday alone and wait to hear from you before we ask Kwame to come over.

Yours,
Hamish Fairweather

messages.text:
Can we hold a short paperwork call for Ellie on the 5th, before the team heads out? She asked how the contract and the right-to-work check fit together when we spoke about the offer on Friday. I’d like to have something to put in the calendar if that’s the easiest way to do it, especially if her first day turns out to be after the offsite.

Luis

Luis Cordero
Lead Product Designer, Acme Studio
3rd floor, 48 Turnmill Street, London EC1M 5RR

Hi Luis,

I’ve sent the contract to Ellie this afternoon. She accepted yesterday and we have Monday 16 November down for her first day, at the £34,000 we offered on Friday. I’ve left the right-to-work instructions in the email with the contract, including how to send the documents directly to People. If she sends anything to you by mistake, please point her back to that email.

I put a private hold in our calendars for 8 am on the 5th, since the Farringdon coach leaves at 8.30. I haven’t invited Ellie to the call. Please leave it that way while I check whether we even need her on a call before the start date.

Hi Luis,

I’ve taken the 8 am call out of the diary. The right-to-work check can go through People before the 16th, and there’s nothing Ellie needs to sit through with us on the morning of the 5th. On Merefurrow, nothing in the contract stops her coming, but she’d be there before she’s on payroll and she should know that. Whether there’s a room for her is Natasha’s call. Please check with Natasha and then answer Ellie yourself.

For the 16th itself, Jake needs a week with the starter form to get the laptop ready, so it has to reach him by the 9th. Please send it to him directly. Lauren can confirm the tool seats once you tell her which ones Ellie needs.

Best,
Shona
